newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor gets court-ordered protection.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor gets court-ordered protection.

text.p: A judge issued an order of protection on Friday for New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and key aides after a local man allegedly made repeated threats to his office.
Christopher Brodeur, 29, was charged with aggravated harassment for making more than 80 telephone calls to Giuliani's office between May and August of last year, authorities said.
Brodeur's threats escalated "beyond mere expressions of anger," Manhattan Criminal Court Justice Judy Levitt said.

According to authorities, Brodeur had a lengthy history of screaming obscenities and making threats to the mayor's office, saying, "You are Nazis. The Mayor should be executed" and "The taxpayers will do the firing squad to you people."
The judge told Brodeur at a court hearing that his remarks were not a matter of free speech.
"You have crossed the line. You have absolutely crossed the line," the judge said.
Brodeur's Legal Aid attorney Mildred Whalen said she knew his statements "sound bad when they are taken out of context. He sends them to everyone he knows.

"It's what most of us think in our heads about politicans but edit out," she said. She said she never thought her client was violent and felt his letters and calls to the mayor were nothing more than "hyperbole."
The order of protection bans Brodeur from making any contact with the mayor, his office or his staff. Such court-ordered warnings often are often issued in cases of harassment or domestic abuse.

In a letter Brodeur sent recently to another judge that was released to reporters, he wrote: "Why is it that Giuliani can threaten drug dealers and cop killers with the death penalty but if I say all corrupt government employees deserve capital punishment, I'm mentally ill and dangerous."
Levitt set a cash bail of $2,000. It was not clear whether Brodeur, who works part-time as a delivery man, carpenter and theatre usher, would be able to raise the money.
Brodeur was arrested March 5. If convicted, he faces more than a year in jail. A hearing is set for March 28.

Brodeur also allegedly sent a postcard to the mayor's press secretary saying: "This is not a threat you stupid drones but if I was ever to open fire on City Hall," he promised to notify newspapers first as to his motives.
He had been arrested four times for harassment, including twice for expressing similiar sentiments to the mayor.
